title: Cassander: adoption-certainty follows justification; not required to obtain it
source_text: XXXVI. Cassander autem jam dictus admittit quidem hanc esse naturam fidei justificantis ut fidelem certum reddat adoptionis suae & reconciliationis cum Deo propter meritum Christi, & sensum divinae gratiae, quem in nobis efficit Spiritus Sanctus, percipiat. Verum haec certitudo remissionis peccatorum nostrorum, juxta ipsum, sequitur justificationem, non vero est aliquid quod requiratur ad illam obtinendam, & sub quo remissio peccatorum nobis promissa sit.
pass_a_gloss: Cassander, already named, does admit that this is the nature of justifying faith: that it makes the believer certain of his adoption and of reconciliation with God on account of Christ merit, and that he perceives the sense of divine grace which the Holy Spirit works in us. But this certainty of the remission of our sins, according to him, follows justification; it is not something required for obtaining justification, or something under which the remission of sins is promised to us.
pass_b_english: Cassander grants that justifying faith naturally yields certainty of adoption and reconciliation, and a sensed grace wrought by the Spirit.
Yet that certainty of remitted sins follows justification; it is not a condition required to obtain justification or under which remission is promised.
